title: Probing fluctuations in photon emission statistics of spin injected quantum dots with time dependent electronic excitation
authors: Chiran Wijesundara, Vincent Iglesias-Cardinale, Yuan Lu, Herbert Fotso, Bo Xu, Tim Thomay
abstract: Electrically spin-injected ensembles of InGaAs/GaAs quantum dots emit circularly polarized single photons, with the emission helicity determined by the spin polarization of the injected electrons. A ferromagnetic CoFeB spin-injection layer with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, combined with an MgO tunnel barrier, enables spin-polarized electron injection into the quantum-dot active region, resulting in circularly polarized photon emission at zero applied magnetic field. These devices realize direct spin-charge-photon conversion in an electrically driven, microelectronics-compatible quantum light source that operates without an external pump laser. Using an extended Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometer with four detectors and time-tagged readout, we measure time-resolved photon-number statistics that resolve up to $|2\rangle$ Fock states within a single excitation cycle. While single-photon ($n=|1\rangle$) emission tracks the electrical excitation pulse as expected, the two-photon ($n=|2\rangle$) statistics exhibit pronounced fluctuations at multiple temporal positions within the pulse. These fluctuations vanish upon demagnetization of the spin-injection layer, establishing a direct link between the multi-photon emission dynamics and the spin polarization of the injected carriers. The observations indicate that spin injection controls not only the helicity of the emitted photons but also higher-order temporal correlations of the emission. The behavior is phenomenologically captured by inserting both a variable excitation mechanism and a set of multi-emitter collapse operators within a stochastic wave function evolution. The platform thus opens a route to electrically driven, spin-controlled single and multi-photon Fock-state sources and provides a testbed for spin-conditioned multi-emitter dynamics in solid-state quantum light sources.
summary: This paper investigates how spin polarization controls the higher-order photon emission statistics from quantum dots. Using time-resolved HBT measurements and advanced simulation, the authors show that two-photon emission exhibits fluctuations directly linked to the spin state of the injected electrons. This opens a pathway for electrically driven, spin-controlled sources of multi-photon Fock states.
main_problem: The study aims to probe the higher-order photon emission statistics from spin-injected quantum dots to understand the underlying multi-emitter dynamics beyond simple second-order correlation measurements.
main_result: Pronounced fluctuations in the two-photon ($|2angle$) emission statistics, which vanish upon demagnetization, establish a direct link between multi-photon emission dynamics and the spin polarization of the injected carriers.
method: The research combines time-resolved, extended Hanbury Brown-Twiss (HBT) interferometry with advanced theoretical modeling using Monte Carlo Wavefunction evolution incorporating joint collapse operators.
model_or_system: The physical system is an ensemble of InGaAs/GaAs quantum dots driven by spin-polarized electron injection from a CoFeB layer. The theoretical model uses a stochastic wave function evolution framework to capture multi-emitter dynamics.
key_observables: Time-resolved photon-number statistics, specifically the counts for $|1angle$ and $|2angle$ Fock states, and the Allan deviation for these photon numbers.
important_parameters: Spin polarization of injected carriers, the excitation pulse profile $\Omega(t)$, and the coupling strength $\kappa$ governing joint emission.
main_assumptions: The model phenomenologically incorporates joint collapse operators that do not arise from standard Weisskopf-Wigner treatments, and the analysis assumes the system can be described by a stochastic wave function evolution.
figures_summary: Figures show time-resolved counts of $|1angle$ and $|2angle$ photons for polarized vs. unpolarized samples, demonstrating fluctuations only in the polarized case. Other figures compare Allan deviations and confirm simulation fidelity across varying excitation pulse shapes.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the experimental setup (HBT/time-tagging) to measure time-resolved photon statistics. It then develops a theoretical model using collapse operators to capture multi-emitter dynamics. Finally, it compares the simulation results against the measured polarization-dependent fluctuations in $|2angle$ photon counts.
why_interesting: This work provides a sophisticated testbed for studying spin-conditioned multi-emitter dynamics in solid-state quantum light sources, moving beyond simple antibunching measurements to characterize higher-order correlations.
